newsitem.title: UK: Dirty tankers flat to weaker, quiet.
newsitem.headline: Dirty tankers flat to weaker, quiet.

text.p: Very large crude carrier (VLCC) 6rates in the Middle East were weaker on Monday, brokers said.
They said the upcoming Eid al-Adha holiday and refinery maintenance in South Korea were dampening trade, and one said he had not heard any VLCC enquiry or fixtures all day.
Another broker pointed to the fixture of the 260,000 tonne Stena Conductor at W47.5 from Kharg Island to the Red Sea for Agip as a sign of significant weakness.
"It looks like they are going to make a meal of it," he said, adding that a vessel of this size would have fetched about W55 on Friday.

"(VLCC) rates are not getting any stronger," said another broker, but added that on other Mideast routes they were little changed from Friday, with voyages west at W50, to Singapore at W50/52.5 and to Japan or South Korea at W57.5/60.
West Africa/U.S. Gulf VLCCs were steady to slightly softer at W70/72.5 in quiet trade while transatlantic rates were unchanged at W65.
The Mediterranean and inter-U.K./Cont markets were likewise lacklustre, with 80,000 crude tonne cargoes at an unchanged W120 and W100 respectively.
Inter-UKC 25,000 tonne fuel oil cargoes were steady at W180/185, and slightly softer in the Med at W195.
"There are few ships looking for cargoes and strong competition (among charterers) in the Med," one broker said.

Caribs/upcoast rates were flat to softer like most of the rest of the market. Crude 70,000 tonne cargoes were fixed at W222.5/225, while 50,000 tonne fuel oil vessels edged down to W190 from W195 on a lack of demand and plenty of ships, brokers said.
